title: Cohort safety canvas & rollout ceremony notes (working)
content:
Purpose
- Lightweight, cross-functional working canvas for planning small-to-medium surface rollouts (canaries + A/B experiments).
- Emphasis: safety-first gating that product, engineering, SRE and CS can use without a heavyweight runbook.

Who this is for
- Product managers running feature experiments or staged launches
- Release engineers / infra owners who wire traffic slices in Console
- Oncall SREs and Observability for guardrail alerts
- Customer Success for major account impact watchlist

High-level flow (ceremony + checkpoints)
1) Pre-read (48h before): owner publishes canvas + short hypothesis, metric list, and rollback plan. Stakeholders: PM, Eng lead, SRE oncall, Observability, CS rep.
2) Kickoff (15–30m): quick alignment: who watches which metric, stop criteria, what ‘normal’ looks like, opt-in/out lists.
3) Launch canary (1–5%): monitor strict guardrails for 30–60 mins or `N` requests threshold.
4) Expand cohorts incrementally (5 -> 25 -> 50% or A/B cohort splits) with explicit gates and timing.
5) Post-mortem / tidy-up: capture learnings, remove flags if feature permanent, or plan rollback post-process.

Ceremony checklist (owner responsibilities)
- Publish pre-read link + short TL;DR: hypothesis, expected direction, primary metric, guardrails, start time window.
- Create a short Slack thread and tag #rollouts-ops + SRE oncall.
- Create a Console rollout config (traffic rule id) and link it in the canvas.
- Ensure metric dashboards pre-made (primary + guardrails) and shared.
- Have a one-click rollback flag defined and owned by Eng-runner.

Metric taxonomy (minimal set)
- Primary (one): conversion or success signal that indicates the feature is working (e.g., model-quality-score, completion-success-rate).
- Guardrails (2–4): latency P95/P99, error rate (5xx/validation-errors), token-cost per request, downstream downstream-API error rate (third-party).
- Signal health (ops): trace volume, logging rate, backpressure/throttling count.
- Secondary/research: user engagement dwell, retention preview signals.

Stop / rollback criteria (examples, conservative first pass)
- Immediate rollback if: new 5xx rate > 0.5% abs increase AND exceeds 3x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Immediate rollback if: P99 latency increases > 300ms (absolute) AND user-facing errors observed.
- Pause expansion if: guardrails degrade but not meeting rollback threshold — hold at current cohort for 1–2 hours, deep-dive.
- Auto-fail expansion if: token-cost per request > 2x expected AND quality delta < +1% (cost > quality).

Traffic partitioning & cohort ideas (practical patterns)
- Randomized stable hashing: user_id % 100 -> cohort (recommended when identity stable).
- Session-based sampling: session_id hash for short lived features (avoid per-request jitter).
- Geo/time slices: use only for region-limited tests, careful with confounding.
- Account targeting: vip customers excluded by default; add allowlist after CS signoff.
- Canary traffic rule pseudocode (console friendly):
  "if request.user_id in cohort_hash_range(0..4): route -> new-feature"

Data checks and sampling thresholds
- Minimum sample for signal detection: rule-of-thumb 1k meaningful events per cohort per day for behavioral metrics. For high-sensitivity model-quality metrics allow smaller if statistically significant; call stats team.
- SLO for alert triage: first guardrail alert owner responds within 15 min; escalate if unresolved after 30 min.

Operational integrations (what Console must expose/monitor)
- Easy traffic slice creation UI + exportable rule id.
- Button to attach current metrics/dashboards and snapshot values.
- Integrated rollback toggle with audit trail and reason picker.
- Canary health view: per-cohort metric comparisons, side-by-side time series, delta bars, and quick links to traces and sample logs.

Communication protocol (quick guide)
- Start: owner posts kickoff message + link to canvas (include timeline and watchlist).
- Watch: SRE/Obs comments initial state within 15 min that canary is green/blocked.
- On alert: use structured message: [ALERT] metric, current val, baseline, cohort size, action required.
- Decision: owner + SRE decide rollback vs hold. If rollback, implement and post status update.

Open questions / design tradeoffs (notes)
- How long to hold at each expansion step? Tradeoff: speed-of-learning vs blast radius. Default suggestion: 30m for latency-only changes, 2h for new-model-quality changes.
- When to include CS in initial canary? Start with CS-watchlist for account-impacting features only.
- Should we automate expansion based on metric thresholds? Initial stance: manual expand with scripted check button in Console; automations later once mature.
- Token-cost vs quality: how to express multi-dimensional tradeoff in an automated gate? Need composite score design (product + econ).

Mini templates (copy-paste for pre-read)
- TL;DR: (one sentence)
- Hypothesis: (one line)
- Primary metric + direction: (metric name, expected delta)
- Guardrails: (list top 3)
- Launch plan: canary % -> expansions -> final cutover window
- Rollback operator & contact: (name + runbook link)

Post-launch tidy and metrics hygiene
- Keep feature flag for at least 24 hours after full expansion to quickly revert if latent regressions.
- Mark dashboards with experiment tag and save a snapshot.
- Run 1-week post-launch quality check and capture any slow regressions in the experiment log.

Quick experiments / low-risk patterns (try these first)
- Background A/B for compute-heavy model changes: collect results but return baseline model until quality validated.
- Shadow evaluation: route to new model but do not surface output; collect metrics.
- Progressive quality gating: use decayed traffic to learning variant while progressively routing production when offline eval passes thresholds.

Notes to self (todo)
- Draft a small Console mock showing the canary health view and one-click rollback.
- Build a test harness for cohort hashing edge cases (null user_id, bots).
- Coordinate with econ on composite cost-quality gate proposal.

References / links
- Linked artifacts above (Confluence canvas, Jira, PR).
- "Experiment design for product teams" (internal deck) — link in Confluence id.

Signature
- Maya Lin (PM, product-console) — working draft, please add comments inline or ping in #rollouts-ops for synchronous discussion.

---
Small, pragmatic, intentionally terse. This is a working canvas: keep it light and iteratively bake into a formal playbook once patterns stabilize.
